verses.text: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you about Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the time I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until today.
Maybe when the people of Judah hear about all the disaster I plan to bring on them, each of them will turn from their evil ways. Then I will forgive their wickedness and their sin."
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on a scroll all the words the LORD had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah told Baruch, "I am restricted. I cannot go into the LORD's temple.

So you go to the LORD's temple on a day of fasting and read the LORD's words from the scroll you wrote as I dictated. Read them to the people there, and to all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.
Maybe they will bring their prayers to the LORD and each turn from their evil ways, because the anger and fury the LORD has announced against these people are great."
Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet told him. He read the LORD's words from the scroll in the LORD's temple.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a time of fasting before the LORD was announced for all the people in Jerusalem and all who came to Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.

Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll to all the people in the LORD's temple. He read them from the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the temple.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the LORD's words from the scroll,

he went down to the secretary's room in the king's palace. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah told them everything he had heard Baruch read to the people from the scroll.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch with this message: "Bring the scroll you read to the people and come here." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and went to them.
They said to him, "Please sit down and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they looked at each other in fear and said to Baruch, "We must tell the king everything."
Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you write all this? Did Jeremiah dictate it?"
Baruch answered, "Yes, he dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."
Then the officials told Baruch, "You and Jeremiah must go and hide. Do not let anyone know where you are."
They left the scroll in the room of Elishama the secretary and went to the king in the courtyard. They told him everything.
The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi brought it from the room of Elishama the secretary. He read it to the king and to all the officials standing beside him.
It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in his winter house, with a fire burning in a fire pot in front of him.
Each time Jehudi read three or four columns, the king cut them off with a knife and threw them into the fire, until the whole scroll was burned up in the fire pot.
The king and his servants heard all these words, but they were not afraid. They did not tear their clothes in sorrow.
Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah even begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
Instead the king ordered Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.
After the king had burned the scroll with the words Baruch had written as Jeremiah dictated, the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Take another scroll and write on it everything that was on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And tell Jehoiakim king of Judah, 'This is what the LORD says: You burned that scroll and said, "Why did you write that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and wipe out both people and animals?"
So this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no descendant to sit on David's throne. His dead body will be thrown out, left in the heat by day and the frost by night.

I will punish him, his children, and his servants for their wickedness. I will bring on them, on the people living in Jerusalem, and on the people of Judah all the disaster I announced against them, because they did not listen.'"

So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it everything that had been on the scroll Jehoiakim king of Judah burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to it.
